title: The rank of a matrix is unchanged by field extension
statement:
Let $K$ and $L$ be fields [def-weil-field] with $K$ a subfield of $L$ (more generally, let $\iota:K\to L$ be a ring homomorphism of fields, necessarily injective, and view a matrix with entries in $K$ as a matrix with entries in $L$ by applying $\iota$ to every entry). Let $m,n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and let $A=(a_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq m,\ 1\leq j\leq n}$ be an $m\times n$ matrix with entries in $K$. For a field $F$ containing $K$, the rank of $A$ over $F$, written $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)$, is the dimension [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] of the $F$-linear span in $F^n$ of the $m$ rows of $A$; this span is a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], spanned by at most $m$ vectors, so $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)\leq\min(m,n)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{rank}_L(A)=\operatorname{rank}_K(A).
$$

Equivalently, a family of rows of $A$ is linearly independent over $L$ if and only if it is linearly independent over $K$.

source.place: Chapter II, §27, proof of Lemma 27.9, last sentence, p. 157 (PDF p. 157, v2.21): 'Obviously, if the condition in (d) is satisfied in K, then it is satisfied in k' (the condition is the vanishing of Hankel determinants, i.e. a rank bound on finite submatrices with entries in k); the same step is Deligne, literature/deligne-weil-I_PMIHES-1974-43.pdf, 'Preuve de (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)', p. 276 (PDF p. 5): 'Cette nullité est vraie dans Q_ℓ si et seulement si elle l'est dans Q'; and the blueprint, literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil1/thm-weil-final-rationality.md, '## Proof': 'every finite Hankel minor has integral entries, so the same rank bound holds over Q'. None of the three writes the linear algebra out.

proof.text: *Step 1: setup.* Since $K$ is a field, the ring homomorphism $\iota:K\to L$ is injective (its kernel is an ideal not containing $1$, hence $0$), so $L$ is a field extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension] and we identify $K$ with $\iota(K)\subseteq L$, hence $K^n\subseteq L^n$ entrywise. Write $r_1,\ldots,r_m\in K^n$ for the rows of the matrix $A$ [def-weil-matrix]; viewed in $L^n$ they are the rows of $A$ regarded as a matrix over $L$. For $F\in\{K,L\}$, $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)$ is by definition [def-weil-matrix-rank] the dimension [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] of the $F$-span $W_F\subseteq F^n$ of $r_1,\ldots,r_m$, a finite-dimensional space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] since it is spanned by $m$ vectors.

II, §7 and §8, or Lang, Algebra, Ch. III §5 and Ch. XIII §4)

proof.text: *Step 2: rank as the largest independent set of rows.* Let $F\in\{K,L\}$ and let $\mathcal I_F$ be the set of subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ such that $(r_i)_{i\in S}$ is linearly independent over $F$; $\emptyset\in\mathcal I_F$. Claim: $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)=\max\{|S|:S\in\mathcal I_F\}$. (a) By [lem-weil-span-independent-subfamily] there is $S_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ with $(r_i)_{i\in S_0}$ linearly independent over $F$ and spanning $W_F$; by [lem-weil-dimension-span-independent-family], $\dim_FW_F=|S_0|$, so $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)=|S_0|\leq\max$. (b) Conversely, for $S\in\mathcal I_F$ the vectors $r_i$, $i\in S$, lie in the finite-dimensional space $W_F$ and are linearly independent there, so $|S|\leq\dim_FW_F=\operatorname{rank}_F(A)$ by [lem-weil-independent-family-card-le-dimension].

proof.text: *Step 3: independence of rows does not depend on the field.* For every $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$, the vectors $(r_i)_{i\in S}$ of $K^n$ are linearly independent over $L$ if and only if they are linearly independent over $K$, by [lem-weil-linear-independence-field-extension] applied to the field extension $K\subseteq L$ and the family $(r_i)_{i\in S}$. Hence $\mathcal I_L=\mathcal I_K$. This is also the 'equivalently' clause of the statement.

proof.text: *Step 4: conclusion.* By Step 2 for $F=L$ and $F=K$ and by Step 3, $\operatorname{rank}_L(A)=\max\{|S|:S\in\mathcal I_L\}=\max\{|S|:S\in\mathcal I_K\}=\operatorname{rank}_K(A)$.
